Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG"
Document applicant: "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd."

These are genuinely different companies. "Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG" is a German entity (GmbH + Co. KG is a German legal form — limited partnership with a GmbH as general partner). "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." is a Japanese entity (Yamanashi is a prefecture in Japan; "Co., Ltd." is a Japanese/Kabushiki Kaisha-style suffix). These are distinct subsidiaries of the Endress+Hauser group.

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

So verdict = different-entity, best_value = "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." (the document's value).

Wait — the rules say the document context includes `<!-- applicant: Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG -->` as a comment, but then the actual certificate text says "Number R85/2008-A-NL1-20.03 revision 4" and doesn't show the applicant in the visible text — the "document" applicant given in the conflict is "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." Hmm, the conflict spec says document = "Endress+Hauser Yamanashi Co., Ltd." I should take the conflict at face value: the document surface (the certificate's own extracted content, perhaps a header elsewhere in the PDF) names the Japanese entity, while the register names the German entity.

These are genuinely different legal entities — same corporate family, but different subsidiaries. Legal-suffix drift rules apply only when the core name is the same. Here "GmbH + Co., KG" vs "Yamanashi Co., Ltd." differ in both suffix AND the core name ("Yamanashi" vs no location, plus "GmbH + Co., KG" is a distinctly German legal form). So different-entity.

The certificate is the legal instrument; the register row may be stale or mis-linked. Best value = the document's value.
